text:
Predicates:
Contains(x, y) ::: x contains y.
Hydrocarbon(x) ::: x is a hydrocarbon.
Alkane(x) ::: x is an alkane.
OrganicCompound(x) ::: x is an organic compound.
ChemicalCompound(x) ::: x is a chemical compound.
Element(y) ::: y is an element.
Mixture(x) ::: x is a mixture.
ContainsOnlyOneElement(x) ::: x contains only one element.
Premises:
∀x (Hydrocarbon(x) → OrganicCompound(x)) ::: All hydrocarbons are organic compounds.
∀x (Alkane(x) → Hydrocarbon(x)) ::: All alkanes are hydrocarbons.
∀x (OrganicCompound(x) → ChemicalCompound(x)) ::: All organic compounds are chemical compounds.
∀x (OrganicCompound(x) → Contains(x, carbon)) ::: All organic compounds contain carbon.
¬∃x (ChemicalCompound(x) ∧ ∀y (Contains(x, y) → y = element)) ::: No chemical compounds contain only one element.
∃x (ChemicalCompound(x) ∧ Contains(x, y) ∧ ContainsOnlyOneElement(x)) ∨ ¬(ChemicalCompound(x) ∧ Contains(x, y) ∧ ContainsOnlyOneElement(x)) ::: The mixture either both is a chemical compound and contains only one element, or neither.
Conclusion:
Contains(mixture, carbon) ::: The mixture contains carbon.
